Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  ABA No. 1312 of 2024  ABA No. 1315 of 2024  ABA No. 1318 of 2024  Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Himanshu Pal, Advocate for the applicants.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, D.A.G. for the State.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. M.K. Ray, Advocate for the informant.
Since all these anticipatory bail applications arise from one and the same FIR, they are taken up together.

Applicants Manish Kumar Aggarwal, Manoj Singhal and Kanchan Jain seek anticipatory bail in FIR No. 539 of 2024, under Sections 120B, 388, 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Bahadrabad, District Haridwar.
According to the FIR, the applicants induced the informant to invest in their project Aarogyam.
They were raising some constructions and building flats.
Nine flats were booked by the informant for which he paid Rs.3.42 crores by taking loans.

But subsequently, the informant came to know that the flats that were booked for him were given into the possession to some other persons and, in fact,
some lodging/hotel services are being run from that premises.
Learned counsel for the applicants would submit that the applicants have not sold any flat.
They could not have sold the flats to some other persons because they were mortgaged with the bank.
It is argued that, in fact, the default of payment was made by the informant.
The flats are not in the possession of any other person.
As and when, the informant pays the remaining amount, he shall be handed over the possession.
It is argued that since the informant has to pay the interest so in order to avoid the payment of interest, FIR has been filed to pressurize the applicants.

1
Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the informant would submit that it is the applicants, who had not kept the promise under the agreement.
It is submitted that the completion of the flats as per the applicants was done on 13.12.2019.

Soon thereafter, the possession was to be given to the informant,
but it is argued that the applicants never offered possession to the informant.
Learned Senior Counsel also submits that the informant had taken loan from the bank.
He is paying interest.
He is looser on either side.
On the one hand, he has to pay interest on the loan amount and on the other hand, he has not been given the possession.
He filed an application to the RERA authorities and also lodged a complaint at Police Station Mohali, in which the notices were served on the applicants in the month of January, 2024.
It is argued that thereafter, in order to make a story, notices were given by the applicants to the informant.
Learned State counsel adopts the argument made by learned Senior Counsel for the informant.
It is a case of business transactions.
There are versions and cross versions.
The applicants say that flats that have been booked by the informant are ready to be delivered to the informant provided he pays the remaining amount.
He has not sold those property.
State to file objections.

Having considered the submissions, as an ad interim measure, till the next date of listing, in the eventuality of arrest, the applicants shall be released on bail subject to their furnishing a personal bond with two sureties by each one of them, each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer ("AO").

In addition to it, the applicants shall also comply with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall co-operate with the investigation.
(ii) The applicants shall not approach any witness in any manner, whatsoever.
(iii) The applicants shall not leave the country without prior permission of the court concerned.
(iv) The applicants shall deposit their passport with the AO.
The passports may only be returned by the order of the court concerned.
In case, the applicants do not have a passport, they shall give an undertaking to that effect to the AO.
(v) The applicants shall also give an undertaking on (i), (ii) & (iii) above.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 10.01.2025 Jitendra ABA/1318/2024 on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80661010/
